transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. What brings you here today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, I guess the main reason I came in is just that I get pulled off track so easily. Like, one Slack ping from a classmate, or a random idea for another project, or even just a song lyric, and suddenly I’ve completely lost the thread of the dashboard I was supposed to be finishing. 

Actually, speaking of song lyrics, I was listening to this amazing playlist my roommate made yesterday—she’s a music major, so she makes these incredibly specific mood playlists, and she added this one band we saw live last summer. We drove like three hours to get to the venue and stopped at this really weird retro diner on the way that had the absolute best milkshakes, but the AC was broken so it was boiling inside... 

Wait, sorry. I totally lost my train of thought. What was I just saying? Oh, right, why I'm here. Yeah, I just... I get sidetracked like that all the time and completely forget what I was actually supposed to be working on.
Have you been feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

No, not really. I mean, I still like doing all the stuff I usually do. Actually, I just started this new intramural volleyball team with some people from my dorm. I've never even played volleyball before, but they needed an extra person because one of the girls sprained her ankle during syllabus week. She tripped over a scooter on the sidewalk—there are so many of those electric scooters everywhere on campus now, it's honestly a hazard. I almost hit one with my bike the other day when I was rushing to my sociology lecture because I slept through my alarm. 

But yeah, I haven't been feeling depressed or anything like that. Just... frustrated that I can't seem to get my stuff done.
Have you ever experienced periods where you felt unusually energetic, needed less sleep, or felt like your thoughts were racing faster than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so? Like, I'm always pretty energetic, I guess. I mean, I definitely don't sleep enough, but that's mostly because I stay up way too late watching TikToks or going down rabbit holes on Wikipedia. Last night I spent like two hours reading about the history of roller coasters. Did you know the first one in America was actually built to transport coal down a mountain? And then people just started riding it for fun. It's wild to think about someone looking at a coal cart and being like, "Yeah, I want to ride that." I actually really want to go to an amusement park soon, but tickets are so expensive, and I'm trying to save money because I need a new laptop for my graphic design class. 

But wait, what did you ask? Oh, right, racing thoughts. I mean, my brain is always kind of going a million miles a minute, but it's not like... an unusual period or anything. It's just my normal.
Have you noticed feeling tired or lacking energy most days, even when you haven’t been physically active?

Not really? I mean, I usually have a lot of energy. Unless I haven't slept, but then I just grab a Celsius from the campus market. They just got this new mango passionfruit flavor, and it is so good, but it's literally always sold out because the lacrosse guys buy them in bulk. I swear I saw one of them carrying three whole cases out of the store yesterday. I don't even know where you'd store that many energy drinks in a dorm room. 

We have those tiny micro-fridges, and mine is completely full of string cheese and leftover dining hall pizza. The pizza here is actually not terrible, surprisingly, especially the white pizza they make on Thursdays... 

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling tired. Yeah, no, I don't really get tired or lack energy during the day. I'm usually pretty on the go.
